aaron.title: Aaron
aaron.about: High Priest living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
aaron.note: Moses's older brother, and the one God sent to do the talking when Moses said he could not. He became Israel's first high priest, and the priesthood ran through his sons after him. Most of the time he is standing next to Moses.

amorite.title: Amorite
amorite.note: One of the peoples in Canaan before Israel came, traced in Genesis 10 to a son of Canaan, and sometimes used loosely for everyone in the hill country. Sihon and Og ruled an Amorite kingdom east of the Jordan that fell to Israel under Moses. Outside the Bible they are the Amurru of Mesopotamian texts, the people whose dynasty produced Hammurabi of Babylon.

babel.title: Babel
babel.note: The plain in Shinar where people, still speaking one language after the flood, set out to build a city and a tower reaching to the heavens and make a name for themselves. God answered by confusing their language.

bashan.title: Bashan
bashan.note: The fertile tableland east of the Jordan, between Gilead and Mount Hermon. Og ruled it, the last of the Rephaim, until Israel beat him and gave the land to half the tribe of Manasseh.

canaan.title: Canaan
canaan.note: The land promised to Abraham and his descendants, roughly modern Israel and the land around it. The conquest under Joshua is that promise, centuries old by then, being kept.

david.title: David
david.about: King living at the time of United Monarchy
david.note: The shepherd from Bethlehem who killed Goliath and became Israel's second king, ruling the largest territory Israel ever held, which Solomon then inherited. Solomon was one of his sons. Nearly half the psalms carry his name, and the Tel Dan inscription, where an enemy king boasts over the house of David, put his dynasty outside the Bible as well.

edom.title: Edom
edom.note: Esau got the byname Edom over a bowl of red stew, and it stuck to the mountain country his descendants settled southeast of the Dead Sea. Bozrah was its old capital and Sela, the Greeks' Petra, its rock fortress. Edom refused Israel passage in the exodus and later helped Babylon sack Jerusalem, and the prophets did not let that go.

egypt.title: Egypt
egypt.note: Joseph rose to power there and kept his family alive through the famine. A later pharaoh enslaved their descendants, and that set up the exodus. For the rest of the Old Testament Egypt stands for the slavery Israel was brought out of, and Matthew has Jesus's family flee there from Herod as if living that story again.

god.title: God
god.note: The Bible never argues that he exists; it assumes it, and Psalm 14:1 calls the man who denies it a fool. The Hebrew is El, from a word meaning strong, or Eloah, far more often in the plural Elohim. The personal name is the four Hebrew letters YHWH, printed LORD in small capitals in most English Bibles; Jehovah is a later hybrid of those letters with the vowels of another word.

hermon.title: Hermon
hermon.note: On Israel's northern border, and the snowmelt off it gives the Psalms their picture of dew. It is near Caesarea Philippi, which makes it a likely site for Jesus's transfiguration.

israel.title: Israel
israel.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
israel.note: God gave Jacob this name after he wrestled through the night at Peniel. It became the name of the nation that came from his twelve sons, and later of the northern kingdom and of the land. For the man himself, see Jacob.

jacob.title: Jacob
jacob.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
jacob.note: Isaac and Rebekah's younger twin, born holding Esau's heel. He bought his brother's birthright for stew, took his father's blessing by a trick, and ran to his uncle Laban, where he worked fourteen years for Leah and Rachel. On the way home he wrestled all night and came away named Israel. He died in Egypt, near Joseph, and was buried at Machpelah as he had asked.

jah.title: Jah
jah.note: A short, poetic form of Yahweh, God's covenant name. It turns up mostly in the Psalms, and it is the end of Hallelujah, "praise Yah".

jerusalem.title: Jerusalem
jerusalem.note: David took it from the Jebusites and made it his capital, and once Solomon's temple stood there it was the centre of Israel's worship for a thousand years. Babylon destroyed it, the exiles rebuilt it, Rome destroyed it again in AD 70. Jesus died and rose just outside its walls, and Revelation ends with a new Jerusalem coming down from heaven.

og.title: Og
og.about: King living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
og.note: King of Bashan and, in Deuteronomy, the last of the Rephaim, with a bed over thirteen feet long. Israel beat him and took his whole kingdom.

pharaoh.title: Pharaoh
pharaoh.note: The king Moses stood in front of. God sent Moses to him to bring Israel out of Egypt, and he hardened his heart through plague after plague before he let them go.

sihon.title: Sihon
sihon.about: King living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
sihon.note: An Amorite king. Israel asked to pass through his land, and he attacked them instead. It cost him his kingdom east of the Jordan.

zion.title: Zion
zion.note: The fortified hill on Jerusalem's southeastern ridge that David took from the Jebusites and called the city of David. He built his palace there. Archaeologists have uncovered the Stepped Stone Structure on that ridge, and many tie it to David's time.
